title: Latency-budgeted shard allocator with residency holdback
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: customers with regional dedicated pools need predictable throughput and low p90 latency while honoring data residency constraints. Current allocator either over-commits cross-region capacity (violating residency) or conservatively pins shards (wasting buffer capacity).

Goal: implement a latency-budgeted shard allocator that reserves a lightweight locality buffer in-region, applies a residency holdback flag to prevent cross-region KV-cache spillover, and cooperates with autoscaler to provide throughput guarantees and a graceful failover path without violating data sovereignty policies.

Scope: allocator algorithm, allocation config surface (policy flags), autoscaler contract changes, safety-drain and spillback behavior, e2e tests, metrics, and rollout playbook. Does not include UI work in Console (follow-up PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Allocator can place shards with an explicit 'residency_holdback' flag that prevents creating cache replicas outside the customer's configured region
P90 inference latency for pinned-residency workloads remains within configured budget (example: 120ms) under nominal load at 80% committed throughput
When a zone becomes unavailable, allocator performs staged spillback to adjacent zones in the same region first; cross-region fallback only occurs when explicitly permitted by customer policy
Autoscaler uses allocator feedback to pre-warm local buffer slots (predictive prewarm) and respects per-customer throughput guarantees
Comprehensive integration test that simulates zone drain and verifies no data is copied to disallowed regions and that throughput degrades gracefully per policy
work_items: Design shard allocator policy language and config schema (policy flags, budgets, holdback toggles)
Implement allocator core: latency-budget accounting, locality buffer lifecycle, allocation scoring function
Autoscaler contract changes: predictive prewarm API and throughput escrow handshake
KV-cache adapter: honor residency_holdback when hydrating or checkpointing cache shards
Safety-drain orchestration: staged drain windows and soft-eviction with throughput escrow release
Add metrics and dashboards: shard-placement decisions, residency-violations (should be zero), prewarm successes/failures, failover path latencies
E2E tests and chaos scenario (zone fail, region fail, transient packet loss), compliance test to assert no cross-region writes
Run internal perf sims and cost modeling; iterate on buffer size defaults
Rollout: canary customers with no-cross-region requirement, monitor for 72h before widening
qa_plan: Unit tests for scoring function and budget accounting
Integration tests with KV-cache emulator to ensure residency_holdback prevents cross-region writes
Load test at committed throughput and at 1.5x burst to validate latency SLOs
Chaos run: simulate zone drain and assert staged spillback happens within SLA windows
rollout_plan: Step 1: deploy to staging, run synthetic traffic and chaos tests
Step 2: enable for 3 internal customers configured for in-region residency (canary) for 72h
Step 3: monitor metrics/dashboards; if no residency violations and latency within budget, expand to select external customers
Rollback: ability to revert allocation decisions and release prewarm buffers; autoscaler will reclaim escrowed throughput
risks: Overly conservative holdback could starve workloads during zone drain, causing customer-visible throttling
Misconfiguration could result in silent cross-region cache writes if KV-cache adapter has a bug
Predictive prewarm mistakes lead to cost spikes; need tunable budget caps and visibility
Complexity in scoring function could increase allocation latency; must keep scoring in the fast path
decisions: Use a two-tier allocation: fast heuristic for steady-state, more expensive rebalancer for background optimization
Residency_holdback implemented at allocator + KV-cache adapter boundary to avoid making cache logic residency-aware alone
Autoscaler will maintain a per-customer throughput escrow that the allocator can borrow against during short drains
Cross-region fallback only allowed when customer's policy explicitly permits 'cross_region_fallback: true'
Default locality buffer size will be conservative (small) and surfaced as a tunable field in Dedicated pool configs
notes: Reviewed trade-offs with SRE and Compliance (meeting notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Residency+Holdback+Review)
Added metric 'residency_holdback.denied_requests' to detect attempted cross-region allocations
PM will own Console UX for new policy toggles in a separate PM ticket
Estimate assumes we can reuse predictive prewarm primitives from ENG-640314; if not, scope will increase
